Resolves #19837

When a test worker ends, the `neuralLink` Playwright fixture now stops the Neural Link Bridge that the worker spawned, and never a Bridge it found running. A worker-scoped auto fixture, `neuralLinkBridge`, applies one rule, `stopSpawnedBridge(connection)`: stop only when `ConnectionService` holds a `bridgeProcess`, which it sets only for a Bridge it spawned itself. The per-test `manageConnection({action: 'start'})` is unchanged, so its reconnect semantics stay. A unit spec pins the rule. Before this, every local e2e run left its Bridge listening on its port (#19837's Context).

Evidence: L3 (real runs of the fixture on this machine at `fd2b75efe6`: a spawned Bridge on an unused port, a failing run, a Bridge already running, plus a red-first control with `origin/dev`'s fixture) → L3 required (AC-1–AC-4 are process-level). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside CI, at `fd2b75efe6`, port 18983 unused before. During the passing run: `npm` 30463 + `node` 30500, process group 30463, listening. 2 s after: no listener, no process from the spawn |
| AC-2 | Outside CI, at `fd2b75efe6`, a deliberately failing test. During: `npm` 32363 + `node` 32407. After: no listener, no process |
| AC-3 | Outside CI, at `fd2b75efe6`, a Bridge started on 18984 before the run (`npm` 31125 + `node` 31151). The test passed through it, and the same PIDs were still listening after the run. CI-covered rule: `unit/test/stopSpawnedBridge.spec.mjs` › "a Bridge found already listening is never stopped" |
| AC-4 | The witnesses above record PID, process group and port before, during and after. The Brain's stop (`bridgeProcess.kill()`, SIGTERM to the `npm` parent) reaped the `node` child in every run, so no Brain leaf is needed |

## Deltas from ticket
The stop rule is an exported helper, `stopSpawnedBridge`, so a unit spec can pin it without a Bridge. The fixture's JSDoc states the one-worker constraint: with several workers on one port, the first to end would stop the Bridge under the others. neo's and Stage's e2e configs both run `workers: 1`.

## Test Evidence
- **Red-first control:** with `origin/dev`'s fixture swapped in, the same passing run left its Bridge listening 2 s after the run (`npm` 27964 + `node` 27996). The committed fixture was restored with `git checkout`.
- **Mutation:** weakening the guard to `if (!connection)` fails the "found already listening" arm (1 failed, 2 passed). Restored.
- **Witness setup:** a zsh script outside the repo polled `lsof` on the port and `pgrep` for `run-bridge.mjs` once per second, filtering each candidate by its cwd. The test files were throwaway specs, deleted and never committed. `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` was a Brain worktree at `fa34303e`.
- `npm run test-unit -- …/stopSpawnedBridge.spec.mjs …/findBridgeScriptRoot.spec.mjs`: 11 passed.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] Stage and the Institution pick this up with the Engine version they pin. After that bump, a local Stage e2e run leaves no Bridge on its port.
